sentences.text: Selmasaurus was a small predatory mosasaur reaching approximately 3 to 5 meters in length.
This animal is classified within the Plioplatecarpinae subfamily, alongside genera such as Angolasaurus and Platecarpus.
It possessed an unusually akinetic skull that could not widen to swallow large prey.
The genus Selmasaurus was officially described by Wright and Shannon in 1988.
A nearly complete skull and partial skeleton were discovered by Steve Johnson and his family in 1996.
The specimen of S. johnsoni was found in the Santonian or Campanian marine horizon of the Niobrara Formation in western Kansas.
Selmasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Santonian to the Campanian stages.
Stable isotope analysis indicates that S. johnsoni was one of the few plioplatecarpines not restricted to nearshore marine environments.
Longrich et al. (2024) recovered Selmasaurus within a monophyletic clade of non-plioplatecarpine plioplatecarpine mosasaurids based on phylogenetic analyses.
